battle.name: 玉壁之戰
battle.brief: 興和二年（546）十一月，東魏高歡率大軍自蒲坂渡河，圍攻河東汾州玉壁。西魏刺史韋孝寬以數千守軍閉城固守，築土山、設飛石、破浮橋、禦雲梯與地道，圍城五十餘日而不下。高歡攻城失利，背生惡瘡而卒，軍退。玉壁未陷，弩機配以矢石、飛石所構成的城頭射擊體系，正是這場僵持得以維持的關鍵。

kit.name: 秦弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，射速遠勝拉弓。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 546年的北魏已裂成東西兩半。534年孝靜帝自洛陽遷都鄴城，東魏定都鄴城，由高歡總攬軍政，國政、兵權與人事都握在他手中；西魏則以長安為都，由權臣宇文泰主持，據關中沃野以自固。兩方隔著黃河、崤山與河東盆地相持，名義上仍共奉北魏孝明帝，行興和二年（西魏大統十二年）年號，實則各自徵兵、各自封爵。玉壁在河東汾州，控著汾水與蒲坂渡口，是東魏由鄴城西出的必經之地，也是西魏關中防線最外層的堡壘。攻方是東魏主力：披甲士卒、騎兵與大批攻城器械自晉陽、鄴城一線南下，統由高歡親領，宿將如斛律金、彭樂各領一部。守方是西魏汾州刺史韋孝寬所部，兵不過數千，卻佔據加固過的城垣，並事先儲備了弓弩、矢石、柴薪與拒馬。東魏靠河東徵發與汾水漕運供應軍糧，西魏則從關中經蒲坂、龍門一線接濟。誰能守住這一段河谷，誰就掌握了下一步西進或東出的主動權。
countriesEn: The empire had already split in two by 546. In 534 Emperor Xiaojing was moved from Luoyang to Ye, where the Eastern Wei took up residence; real power in the east lay with Gao Huan, who controlled the court, the army and every appointment, while the Western Wei held Chang'an under the regent Yuwen Tai, resting on the fertile Guanzhong plain. The two states faced each other across the Yellow River, the Xiaoshan range and the Hedong basin, and both still pretended to serve the same Northern Wei emperor Xiaoming under the same era name — Xinghe in the east, the Western Wei's Daotong twelfth year in the west — yet each levied its own troops and ennobled its own men. Yubi sat in Fuzhou prefecture of Hedong, commanding the Fen River and the Puban ford: the road any eastern army had to take to reach the west, and the outermost fortification of the Western Wei's Guanzhong line. The besiegers were the main Eastern Wei host, armoured infantry, cavalry and a large train of siege engines drawn south from Jinyang and Ye under Gao Huan in person, with veteran commanders such as Hulü Jin and Peng Le leading detachments. The defenders were the troops of Wei Xiaokuan, governor of Fuzhou, no more than several thousand men, but they held a reinforced wall and had laid up in store crossbows, arrows, stones, firewood and caltrops. The East drew grain and river transport along Hedong; the West sent supplies from Guanzhong through Puban and Longmen. Whoever held this stretch of river valley held the initiative for the next move, east or west.
people: 高歡（496年—546年）出身渤海高氏，起家於爾朱榮的部曲，靠掃平河北爾朱氏勢力迅速擴張，534年高歡奉孝靜帝遷都鄴城並自居丞相、錄尚書事，東魏實權盡歸其手。他用兵狠而多變，546年卻把全部家當押在一座堡壘上：自蒲坂濟河後直趨玉壁，圍城五十餘日，屢用新造攻城器械，屢被韋孝寬破解，僵持不下，最終背生惡瘡（疽發背）而死，年五十。韋孝寬是西魏這場守城戰的主角，京兆杜陵人，早年以鎮壓地方亂兵與守禦兗州見長，546年以汾州刺史身份獨守玉壁，破浮橋、壘土山、禦雲梯、焚地道、夜襲敵營；高歡病亡後東魏軍退，他仍率騎追擊，直抵鄴城近郊，斬獲甚眾。斛律金是東魏宿將，高歡病後仍督眾攻城，主力終因喪主而退。宇文泰坐鎮關中，調兵策應，穩住西魏全局。高歡死後，其子高澄秘不發喪，佯報大捷而退兵。西魏朝廷隨後為韋孝寬加官進爵，此人自此列名北周一代名將。
peopleEn: Gao Huan (496–546) came from the Gao clan of Bohai and had risen through the army of Erzhu Rong; by sweeping away the Erzhu power in Hebei he had built a following of his own, and in 534 he escorted Emperor Xiaojing to Ye and took the posts of chancellor and recorder of the imperial secretariat, leaving the Eastern Wei in his hands. He was a hard, inventive commander, fond of wearing an enemy down in a series of attacks, and in 546 he staked everything on a single fortress: crossing the Yellow River at Puban he drove straight for Yubi, and for more than fifty days threw new siege engines at a wall that Wei Xiaokuan kept neutralising, until a carbuncle broke out on his back and killed him in his fiftieth year. Wei Xiaokuan was the man who decided the siege. A native of Duling in the Jingzhao region, he had made his name suppressing local revolt and defending Yanzhou, and in 546, as governor of Fuzhou, he held Yubi alone — breaking the pontoon bridge, raising earthen countersworks, checking the assault ladders, burning the saps, raiding the enemy camp by night. When Gao Huan died and the eastern army pulled back, Xiaokuan still mounted a pursuit that reached the outskirts of Ye and took a heavy toll. Hulü Jin was the Eastern Wei veteran who kept the siege going while the commander was ill; the army finally withdrew for want of a master. Yuwen Tai, seated at Guanzhong, moved troops to cover the western capital and kept the Western Wei steady throughout. After his father's death Gao Cheng concealed the news, announced a great victory and withdrew the army. The Western Wei court then raised Wei Xiaokuan in office and nobility, and his name would one day stand among the famous generals of Northern Zhou.
kits: 這場戰爭的技術核心是弩。城頭陳列的秦弩一類弩機，以機牙蓄力、望山定瞄，張弦全憑腰臂之力，一發既中，精度遠勝步弓；有效射程約在一百五十至二百步上下，遠足以壓住城下百步內的攻城器械與集結兵力，射速又足以在對方靠近之前連續打散隊形。守軍在城上分區配置弓弩，每一具備足數十支箭，箭矢總量以萬計，專待雲梯、土山與衝撞車進入射界即發。破浮橋靠的是弩箭先擊其支柱，再以火焚燒；對方築土山逼近，守方就築更高的土山與木樓居高反擊，弓弩自上而下專射攀城士卒；敵造雲梯、飛樓，守方以長戟與弩交叉封住梯口；敵鑿地道，守方反挖坑道，填柴焚燒，以火煙反制；敵夜襲並企圖在城頭架設竹馬，守軍則以長戟刺穿。攻城方除雲梯、撞車、橫車、飛樓、塹車外，還備飛石砲一類拋擲機，以及壕壘與鹿角拒馬；糧秣靠牛車、馬匹與汾水漕運，騎兵負責側翼與追擊，兩軍皆以鐵甲為主。玉壁一役之後，弩砲合一的守城體系在北方城防中被視為標準配備。
kitsEn: The technical heart of this war was the crossbow. Crossbow locks of the Qin type were mounted on the walls: the lock held the strain in its trigger mechanism, the sight arm gave the aim, and drawing the string took the full strength of a man's back and arms. One shot, one hit, far more accurate than a war bow, and with an effective range of roughly one hundred fifty to two hundred paces it out-reached the ground the assault engines and the massed troops needed to cross, while its rate of fire was enough to break up formations before they closed. The defenders distributed bows and crossbows along the wall by sector, kept scores of bolts for each weapon, and counted the arrows in store by the tens of thousands, holding them for the moment when ladders, earthen ramps and battering rams crossed the killing ground. The pontoon bridge fell to crossbow fire on its trestles and then to fire; when the enemy built earthen ramps to close the distance, the defenders raised higher earthworks and timber towers above them and shot down at the men climbing; assault ladders and flying towers were met with long spears and crossbows crossed over the parapet; saps were answered with counter-mines filled with firewood and lit, so that smoke and flame drove out the diggers; and the night attack, with its bamboo horse, was met with the long spear. On the attacking side, alongside assault ladders, rams, wheeled battering cars, flying towers and screening carts, the East had its stone-throwing engines and its ditch-and-caltrop line; grain moved by ox-cart, by horse and by barge on the Fen, cavalry covered the flanks and pursued the defeated, and both armies fought in iron armour. After Yubi the combination of crossbow and stone engine became standard issue for the fortified towns of the north.
tactics: 攻守雙方都清楚：這不是野戰，而是一場工程與射擊的消耗。東魏選擇不分散兵力，把所有攻城器械集中於玉壁城南一處倚城而建，每攻一輪即撤換疲兵，騎兵則繞城搜尋糧道與薄弱之處；韋孝寬的應對是把城牆當成弩的射擊平台：先以火攻加弩箭毀掉汾水浮橋，切斷敵軍陸路進逼與器械前移的通道，再築兩座土山與敵土山對峙，弓弩居高臨下封住土山頂端；敵人進到弩的射程之內，守方以連續弩箭射擊其扛夫與操作手，逼迫攻城器械停在毫無遮蔽的開闊地上；雲梯靠牆的一瞬間，弩手壓制梯腳，長戟手揮戟斫落梯上士卒；地道則由坑道反制，填入柴薪點火，用煙火燒傷挖掘者。夜裡守方不只防守：韋孝寬曾派兵夜襲敵營，砍斷承載雲梯的竹竿，斬殺敵方督將與數百士卒，使高歡右膝中箭而不得不一度罷攻城具。整場包圍戰，誰先把投射物密度與進攻節奏調到對方忍受不了，誰就會先崩。最終垮掉的是攻城方：器械、士氣與主將的病體三者同時崩解，隊伍在嚴冬裡自行瓦解退走。
tacticsEn: Both sides understood that this was not a battle of manoeuvre but a contest of engineering and shooting worn down over time. The Eastern Wei chose not to spread its force: every siege engine was concentrated in one place against the south side of the city, men were rotated after each assault so that fresh troops replaced spent ones, and cavalry rode around the walls hunting the grain road and the thin spots. Wei Xiaokuan's answer was to treat the wall as a platform for the crossbow. First he destroyed the pontoon bridge over the Fen with fire and crossbow fire, cutting the enemy's dry approach and the track along which engines could be brought forward; then he raised two earthen countersworks against the enemy's earthwork so that the bows stood above it and sealed the crest. When the attackers came within range the defenders poured crossbow bolts at the porters and the men working the engines, forcing the machines to stand in the open where nothing covered them; at the instant a ladder touched the wall the crossbowmen fixed the ladder's feet and spearmen cut down the men on it; and saps were answered with counter-mines filled with firewood and lit, so that smoke and flame drove out the diggers. At night the defenders did not merely hold: Xiaokuan sent men into the enemy camp to cut the bamboo poles carrying the ladders, killing an enemy officer and several hundred of his men and wounding Gao Huan in the right knee, which obliged him to suspend his engines for a time. In a siege of this kind, whoever first pushed the density of missiles and the tempo of assault past the enemy's endurance would break first. In the end it was the besiegers who broke: engines, morale and the failing body of the commander failed together, and the army dissolved in the winter cold and withdrew.
data: 關於兵力數字，史書說法彼此出入，只能取其大略：高歡自蒲坂濟河後投入玉壁方向的兵眾，多數記載在十萬以上，軍中傳稱二十萬，另有精騎數千至萬餘的騎兵隊伍記載；韋孝寬一方守軍只有數千人，靠城垣與預儲器械硬撐。圍城歷時五十餘日，自十月屯兵到十一月軍退約兩個月，期間東魏屢次更換攻城器械，土山、雲梯、撞車、飛樓逐次上陣，器械與士卒折損累積，卻始終未能合圍。數字上最確定的一條是高歡的年齡：卒時五十歲，遺令秘不發喪。按當時的度量，弩的殺傷距離約一百五十至二百步，一座中等城堡的守軍通常要備數十具弩機、上百具弓與數萬支箭，箭矢在五十餘日的射擊中消耗極快，因此守方還需同時儲存柴薪、拒馬與石彈。戰後東魏撤退時大批攻城器械被毀棄焚燒，韋孝寬追擊至鄴城近郊，斬獲與俘獲的數目史籍未詳記確數，只言斬獲甚眾。
dataEn: On the numbers, the histories disagree and only the broad strokes can be used. The force Gao Huan committed to Yubi after crossing at Puban is recorded in most accounts at more than a hundred thousand, with a figure of two hundred thousand current in the camp, and separate mentions of cavalry detachments numbering from several thousand to over ten thousand; the defenders under Wei Xiaokuan were only a few thousand men, held together by the wall and by stores laid up in advance. The siege ran for more than fifty days, roughly two months from the investment in the tenth month to the withdrawal in the eleventh, and the Eastern Wei brought up its engines in turn — earthen ramps, ladders, battering cars, flying towers — with losses in machines and men accumulating steadily and no close cordon ever achieved. The one firm figure is Gao Huan's age: he died in his fiftieth year, ordering that the news be kept secret. By the measurements of the time a crossbow killed at roughly one hundred fifty to two hundred paces; a middling fortress would stock dozens of crossbow locks, a hundred or more bows and tens of thousands of bolts, and such a supply drains fast under fifty days of shooting, which is why the defenders also laid in firewood, caltrops and stone shot. When the Eastern Wei withdrew, much of the siege train was destroyed and burned on the spot; Xiaokuan's pursuit reached the outskirts of Ye, and though the histories give no exact count of the killed and taken, they say only that the capture was very great.
cause: 東西魏分立之後，河東是爭奪的重心。東魏倚仗河北的人力物力與鄴城的地利，卻被西魏的關中與更西邊的涼州、雍州隔在以東，河西走廊與西域商路又遠在西魏一方；高歡要打通東西，唯一可走的路是沿汾水河谷南下，先取河東，再過蒲坂入關中。玉壁正是這條路上最堅的一枚釘子：它卡在汾水東岸通往蒲坂的窄道旁，城池不高卻極為牢固，附近有汾水可取水、可築營，牆前又有開闊地可供展開器械。西魏派韋孝寬鎮守此城，正是看準了這一層——只要玉壁不破，東魏的西路大軍就只能停在汾州南面。開戰的直接契機是高歡自蒲坂渡河成功，東魏得以把全部攻城器械運過天險，兵鋒直指玉壁。高歡此前已在河陽一役中擊敗西魏，士氣正盛，加上宇文泰久居關中、以逸待勞，高歡不願再給對方更多整備時間，遂集中全部兵力孤注一擲。
causeEn: Once the empire was divided, the Hedong basin became the prize. The Eastern Wei had the manpower and material of Hebei and the position of Ye, but the Western Wei held Guanzhong in the west and, beyond it, Liangzhou and Yongzhou with the corridor to the Western Regions and the trade that went with it. The only road that could link east to west ran down the Fen valley: take Hedong first, then cross at Puban into Guanzhong. Yubi was the hardest nail on that road. It sits beside the narrow track from the east bank of the Fen towards Puban, its walls not tall but extremely solid, with the river at hand for water and for the besiegers' camp, and open ground before the rampart on which to lay out engines. The Western Wei had posted Wei Xiaokuan there for exactly that reason: while Yubi held, an eastern army on the western road could go no further than the line south of Fuzhou. The immediate occasion was Gao Huan's crossing of the Yellow River at Puban, which let the Eastern Wei bring every engine over the natural barrier and point the army at Yubi. Gao Huan had already beaten the Western Wei at Heyang, morale was high, and Yuwen Tai sat back in Guanzhong waiting for the enemy to tire himself out. Rather than give the West more time to prepare, Gao Huan concentrated everything and threw it at one wall.
impact: 玉壁保住的不只一座城。河東汾線從此仍在西魏手中，東魏西進的第一道大門關了起來，西魏得以安心在關中整軍、興屯田、與東魏長期對峙；高歡的西征計畫也隨着他的死而中止，東魏的戰略重心此後轉向河南與江淮。玉壁更深的影響在高歡之死本身：他一病不起，東魏內部的權力交接立刻變得兇險，子高澄與諸將的猜忌、與河南侯景的變亂，幾年後釀成侯景之亂，把梁朝打得支離破碎；侯景既叛梁，終又降西魏，使西魏不得不把大軍壓在江漢前線，替北周的南下爭取到十餘年的喘息時間。一場守城戰改變了南北兩個王朝的運勢，這在十六國南北朝史上並不多見。技術上，玉壁也驗證了當時的攻城極限：重裝器械——雲梯、飛樓、撞車與地道——在守方配備飛石、弓弩、坑道與火攻的堅城面前，得不償失，弩砲合一的守城方式自此在北方城防中站穩。
impactEn: What Yubi preserved was more than a wall. The Fen line in Hedong stayed in Western Wei hands, the first great door on the east's road west was shut, and the Western Wei could settle down in Guanzhong to muster, farm and face the East in a long stalemate; Gao Huan's plan of conquest died with him, and Eastern Wei strategy turned south towards Henan and the Yangtze. The deeper effect lay in that death itself: with Gao Huan bedridden, the transfer of power in the Eastern Wei turned treacherous at once, and the suspicion between his son Gao Cheng and the generals, together with the revolt of Hou Jing in Henan, boiled over a few years later into the Hou Jing rebellion, which broke the Liang court apart. Having turned on Liang, Hou Jing finally surrendered to the Western Wei, forcing it to press a great army onto the Jianghan front and so buying Northern Zhou a decade or more of breathing room. A single siege thus changed the fortunes of two southern and northern courts at once, which is rare in the history of the Sixteen Kingdoms and the Northern and Southern dynasties. In technical terms Yubi also marked the limit of what siegecraft could then achieve: heavy machines — ladders, flying towers, battering rams and saps — cost more than they gained against a strong wall furnished with stone engines, crossbows, counter-mines and fire, and the combined crossbow-and-stone-engine defence of the period established itself in the fortified towns of the north.
result: 玉壁沒有陷落。東魏攻了五十餘日，土山被壓、浮橋被燒、雲梯被斫、地道被反挖，高歡本人又染背疽而死，攻城器械大批損壞，士氣耗盡，隊伍在十一月自行撤退。守將韋孝寬守住城，等敵退兵後又率騎兵追擊，追到鄴城近郊，斬獲甚眾，自己一方折損有限。西魏不僅沒有丟失河東，反而因這場勝仗穩住了關中屏障，韋孝寬加官進爵，列名當世名將；高歡一死，東魏的西征中止，此後十餘年再無同等規模的深入關中之舉，直到侯景之亂把東魏的注意力整體拖向南方。從兵器史的角度看，這場戰爭也留下一篇教科書式的守城戰記：秦弩配以矢石、飛石砲與坑道火攻，把一座中等城堡變成了東魏重裝攻具的殺場，證明了弩機在城防體系中的樞紐地位。
resultEn: Yubi did not fall. The Eastern Wei had assaulted for more than fifty days; the earthen ramp was suppressed, the pontoon bridge burned, the ladders cut down, the saps counter-mined, and Gao Huan himself was killed by a carbuncle on his back, so the engines were lost in numbers, the morale drained, and the army withdrew of its own accord in the eleventh month. The garrison held the city, and when the enemy pulled out Xiaokuan mounted a pursuit that reached the outskirts of Ye and took a heavy toll, while his own losses stayed limited. The Western Wei had not merely kept Hedong: it had won a victory that stabilised the Guanzhong screen, Wei Xiaokuan was raised in office and nobility and entered the roll of the age's great commanders, and with Gao Huan dead the western campaign of the Eastern Wei ended — for more than a decade there was no comparable drive into Guanzhong, until the Hou Jing rebellion pulled the whole attention of the eastern state southward. In the history of arms the siege also left a textbook account of defensive warfare: crossbows worked with arrow-stone, stone-throwing engines and counter-mines lit by fire turned a middling fortress into a killing ground for the East's heavy machines, and confirmed the crossbow lock as the pivot of the whole system of city defence.
